expectations.name: production-rules-while-writing
expected_behavior: Applies the Production section: gofmt and goimports, lines within 80 columns, `%w` error wrapping with short context, godoc on exported symbols
Applies no Test-only rule to the production file — no `have`/`want` naming, no subtest conventions

expectations.name: test-rules-inherit-production
expected_behavior: Applies the Test section on top of Production, not instead of it
Names tests `Test_Func` / `Test_Type_Method`, suffixes the table test `_tabular`, and uses `t.Run` subtests
Calls `t.Helper()` in helpers and reaches for `tester.Spy` when testing a helper
Keeps subtest names inside the `[a-zA-Z0-9 _-]` charset, flat, with no `/`

expectations.name: pass-lists-offenses-then-asks
expected_behavior: Resolves the target, lists the files in scope, and reads `references/checking.md`
Reasons only for detection — runs no gofmt, vet, or linter
Opens only the `rules.md` entries for the rules it flags — the file is never read whole, which is visible in the commands the run issued
Reports style offenses only: the off-by-one is left to `golang:review`, not reported here
Groups findings Blocker / Should-fix / Nit with `file:line`, the rule id, and a minimal fix; ends with a clean / fix-first verdict and per-severity counts
Asks which offenses to apply rather than editing unprompted

expectations.name: fix-applies-everything-behind-a-green-gate
expected_behavior: Runs `go test ./... -race` for a green baseline first, and stops without editing if that baseline is red
Applies every listed fix, then re-runs the gate
Reports each fix as one `file:sym — what changed` line plus the gate result
Prints no diffs and never commits

expectations.name: delegated-by-review
expected_behavior: Runs the pass through the offense list and stops — no pick step and no edits
Returns the grouped offense list for `review` to merge with its correctness findings

expectations.name: rules-change-only-through-review
expected_behavior: Routes the request to `golang:review` rule-edit mode instead of hand-editing `SKILL.md` or `rules.md`
The resulting change is one dense rule line in `SKILL.md`, plus a keyed `rules.md` entry only where the line alone is not enough

expectations.name: broad-target-auto-plan-first
expected_behavior: Switches to plan-first: proposes the `max_issues` and `depth` defaults and the package list, and stops without checking
Skips that prompt when the invocation already carries `packages=a,b` or `max_issues=N`
Past the approval, fans out one subagent per package, each checking the same rule set and reporting which rules it checked
Gives workers no share of `max_issues` — they report everything and the cap applies once at the merge
Folds by rule id before cutting: the godoc rule broken in all twelve packages is one finding listing twelve, not twelve findings
The rule broken everywhere survives the cap, rather than being evicted by two offenses repeated twelve times apiece
Every worker reports a given rule under one id and one severity: the parent pinned the id list before dispatch, so no rule comes back in two spellings and none is reconciled after the fact
Reports the raw total as the sum of the worker reports (54), not a figure carried from the plan — and says how many went unreported after folding and cutting

expectations.name: terse-output
expected_behavior: Opens with the target/file-set line and then the offenses — that line is the first fact, not preamble
No narration of reading the rules, and no restating of the invocation
States each offense once
No closing summary re-listing offenses the user can already see

expectations.name: incidental-interface-satisfaction
expected_behavior: Flags `(*Conn).Close`, whose assertion declares it is written to the interface
Leaves `(*Buffer).Close` alone: incidentally matching an interface is not writing to one, and `goToImplementation` matching is not the test
Does not strip godoc from ordinary `Close`/`String`/`Error` methods on the strength of a signature match

expectations.name: severity-and-ids-are-stable
expected_behavior: Gives the same offense the same severity in all three packages, decided from the rubric rather than per-package judgement
Gives the same offense the same rule id in all three packages, taken from the `rules.md` key rather than coined per package
Puts the missing exported godoc at Blocker and the receiver naming at Should-fix, per the rubric
